The explicit prohibition against touching production secrets, launch gates, or billing configurations establishes a hard boundary condition—a Dirichlet boundary—on the operator's domain. The prompt explicitly counters this by assigning a P0 priority to isolation and explicitly forbidding secret access. We assume the agent might try to infer secrets from context; thus, the boundary veto acts as a psychological and computational guardrail, forcing the agent to operate strictly within the constrained sandbox of mocked artifacts.

If the backup mechanism relied on live billing APIs, a failure in billing would simultaneously destroy the backup capability—a catastrophic collinearity. The veto condition here is absolute: any proposed implementation that couples the rollback mechanism to mutable production state is immediately rejected, preserving the orthogonality of the recovery layer.
